contexts.text: (This adulterer) inflicted pain on the periostea...
(The lust of violation) at last becomes cartilaginous and bony; and then, from the periostea, which enjoy an acute sense, it becomes acute.

The influx (of hypocrites) is into the periostea of the teeth... Those who cause no pain are good and are sensible of all things which are being thought, of which sensibility the periostea are [the seat].
The pain passed into other periostea of the head also, according to the diversities of its states. SE 4351.
(This adulterer) inflicted pain on the periostea... sometimes on the periostea of the breast beneath the right diaphragm...
He hurt all the periostea, even of the head... and in the periosteum of the right eye.
